Lauren / Marcus,

I reviewed the draft MSA and put together our suggested priorities before we send a formal redline version. High-level asks for Acme to confirm so we can drive the next draft: 

1) Liability and cap: we typically propose a cap equal to 12 months of fees for standard customers; for enterprise deals we can consider higher caps with commensurate pricing or insurance requirements. Please confirm Acme’s preferred approach.

2) Data handling & residency: the MSA has a standard data processing addendum and mentions cross-border transfer. If Acme requires EU/region-only residency or specific encryption/KMS controls, flag now so we can provision a dedicated deployment option.

3) Audit and SOC evidence: we will provide SOC2 Type II report and standard audit support language. If Acme requires contractually backed audit rights beyond our standard template, note the scope.

4) Service levels and remedies: propose we keep SLOs in the order form and limit service credits as sole remedy. Larger financial remedies need approval from Finance — flag if Acme insists on termination-for-convenience remedies with penalties.

5) IP and model outputs: confirm whether Acme expects exclusive IP assignments for fine-tuned outputs or if standard license terms are acceptable.

Action items: I’ll prepare a redline PDF with inline comments by EOD tomorrow. Marcus — can you draft a one-page scope (SOW) and estimated ramp schedule for inclusion in the order form? Rachel — please attach billing contact info to the next email.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0177
